bull_case: Value-added services, cross-border growth and sustained buybacks can keep per-share cash compounding in the low-double digits, supporting the Bull path.
bear_case: Higher customer incentives, regulation/litigation and slower payment-volume growth could push owner-FCF/share growth toward low single digits and compress terminal value.
thesis: Mastercard remains a high-quality payment network, but the frozen price already requires roughly 10.0% annual owner-FCF/share growth for ten years under the locked 9%/20x Base policy. The modeled Base value is $520.71, below the $565.24 price, while Bull remains materially above price. The expectation gap is therefore limited rather than absent.

evidence.source: deterministic valuation from frozen company_context and locked calibration policy

evidence.claim: TTM owner-FCF proxy after PP&E capex and capitalized software is about $15.975B, or $17.85/share.
H1 2026 net revenue grew 15% reported / 12% currency-neutral; value-added services and solutions grew 21% reported / 18% currency-neutral.
H1 2026 customer rebates and incentives in the payment network rose 22% reported / 19% currency-neutral.
At the frozen price of $565.24, the locked 20x Base DCF requires about 10.0% constant annual owner-FCF/share growth for ten years.
evidence.source: reverse DCF using locked harness policy

counterevidence: The H1 operating-cash-flow comparison is depressed by customer-incentive payments and litigation-settlement cash timing, so a single TTM cash-flow window can understate normalized economics.
Mastercard's value-added services are growing materially faster than payment-network revenue, which can support a longer growth runway than a mature card-network framing implies.
Aggressive repurchases reduce the diluted share base and can lift owner-FCF/share faster than aggregate owner FCF.
The Base terminal fraction is about 67%, so terminal assumptions remain economically important even though they are below the harness's 80% review threshold.
unknowns: Five-year own-history valuation percentile is not frozen in company_context.
Long-run customer-incentive intensity and its effect on payment-network net revenue.
Long-run regulatory/interchange/routing economics across major jurisdictions.
Sustainable contribution of value-added services to consolidated margins and reinvestment returns.
falsifiers: If owner-FCF/share compounds materially below high-single digits while incentives continue to outgrow underlying network revenue, the Base case is too optimistic.
If regulation causes a durable deterioration in network take economics that cannot be offset by volume/VAS growth, the Base and Bull paths fail.
If buybacks cease to reduce the share count at economically sensible prices, expected per-share compounding weakens.
